title: Bar Kada

paragraphs: Mentioned at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Peah 7:2: “Bar Kada—Rabbi Abbahu said.” Hyman cites Penei Moshe’s explanation that this is a sage’s name.

notes.text: The frozen locator combines chapter7 with ספ״ב; its latter abbreviation is left unresolved. The consulted Peah7:2 paragraph contains Bar Kada and Rabbi Abbahu, but does not by itself establish how to parse Hyman’s compressed report formula or his locator. Penei Moshe’s interpretation is attributed to Hyman’s notice.

The saved named Guggenheimer Peah chapter 7, last scalar of its second halakhah, has Abbahu in the name of Shimon ben Lakish, then בר כדה, then “Abbahu said.” It does not itself establish Bar Kada as a reporter. The earlier bracketed “[reported]” is therefore withdrawn. Supplied ספ״ב remains literal; the digital location supports an end-of-halakhah-2 comparison. Penei Moshe’s sage-name explanation remains Hyman’s attribution, without a fresh commentary inspection.

Hyman (vol. I, p. 286) prints ספ״ב. The passage stands at the end of halakhah 2 in the Guggenheimer edition. The consulted Penei Moshe (Piotrków edition) explicitly takes Bar Kada as a person who relayed the explanation in Rabbi Abbahu’s name. Guggenheimer’s translation instead takes the expression to mean the remainder of the harvest. The English keeps Hyman’s compressed quotation.
